Daily Brief

Sunday's global developments are dominated by pivotal elections across multiple continents. Serbia holds its most contested parliamentary vote in 14 years, with a student-led movement posing an unprecedented challenge to President Vučić after nearly two years of anti-corruption protests [BBC, France 24]. Brazil's runoff election sees incumbent President Lula facing right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro in a race polls show as neck-and-neck, with implications for US-Latin America relations under Trump [BBC, FT, Al Jazeera]. In France, more than 400,000 protesters took to the streets over cost-of-living concerns, with nearly 1,000 arrests following clashes between demonstrators and police in Paris and other cities—though authorities largely prevented a repeat of last weekend's severe disorder [BBC, RFI, Globe and Mail]. The Ebola outbreak continues to spread concern as Nigeria confirms its first case in over a decade, with conflicting accounts from Uganda and Switzerland complicating efforts to trace the source of infection [Guardian]. Meanwhile, Elon Musk confirmed SpaceX restricted Ukraine's Starlink access, citing terms-of-service violations, with service reportedly restored after President Trump's intervention [BBC].

Top Stories
01 Geopolitics

Serbia Votes in Closest Election in 14 Years as Student Movement Challenges Vučić

  • Serbian voters are choosing among 18 parties for the 250-seat parliament, with polling showing President Aleksandar Vučić's Serbian Progressive Party neck-and-neck with the student-backed Students' List
  • The student movement emerged from nearly two years of protests following the 2024 collapse of a railway station canopy in Novi Sad that killed 16 people
  • The Students' List selected 250 candidates through university faculty assemblies, with Novi Sad University professor Ilija Srdanović heading the list
  • High turnout is expected, which could push smaller parties below the 3% threshold needed for parliamentary representation

02 Geopolitics

Brazil's Runoff Election Pits Incumbent Lula Against Flávio Bolsonaro in Tight Race

  • President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, 80, seeks an unprecedented fourth term against Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, 45, son of imprisoned former president Jair Bolsonaro
  • Flávio Bolsonaro led the first round on October 4, marking the first time an incumbent has trailed going into the runoff
  • Bolsonaro campaigned on cracking down on organized crime, cutting taxes and public spending, and pledged to release his father from prison
  • Nearly 160 million Brazilians are eligible to vote, with polls closing at 8pm GMT

03 Society

Nearly 1,000 Arrested as Cost-of-Living Protests Sweep France for Second Weekend

  • Between 410,000 (government estimate) and 800,000 (union estimate) people protested across France over cost of living, school funding, and fuel prices
  • Police deployed 70,000 officers with armored vehicles, helicopters, and water cannon; clashes erupted in Paris, Marseille, and Bordeaux after largely peaceful daytime marches
  • President Macron restricted demonstrations to those organized by recognized trade unions; hundreds have been jailed through fast-track court hearings
  • Authorities largely prevented a repeat of last weekend's widespread rioting and looting, described as among the worst disorder in France's modern history

04 Technology

Musk Confirms SpaceX Restricted Ukraine's Starlink, Says Service Restored After Trump Intervention

  • Elon Musk confirmed SpaceX restricted Ukraine's Starlink satellite internet service, accusing Ukraine's military of violating terms of service by using it for offensive drone strikes
  • Ukraine said the restrictions hampered defensive operations for more than a week, limiting drone speeds to 161km/h; service now reportedly allows speeds above 400km/h
  • President Trump said he told Musk to 'put it back' after initially denying he had instructed any limitation
  • Musk denied responsibility for simultaneous issues with Starshield, the US military-grade counterpart, suggesting the Pentagon could be responsible

05 Society

Ebola Outbreak Reaches Nigeria as Conflicting Accounts Complicate Contact Tracing

  • Nigeria confirmed its first Ebola case in over a decade: a woman in Abuja who began showing symptoms on October 7 and tested positive after hospital admission
  • Switzerland said the patient, a Ugandan-born wife of a Swiss diplomat, had not traveled to DR Congo and likely contracted Ebola in Uganda; this contradicts Uganda's earlier claim she had traveled to eastern DR Congo
  • Uganda insists it has no active Ebola cases and was declared Ebola-free by WHO in August; Africa CDC is investigating possible contact with a Kenyan Ebola patient at Entebbe airport
  • The outbreak, first detected in DR Congo in May, has now spread to Uganda, Kenya, and Nigeria, making it the most geographically widespread in history
